The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement, not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University.


For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements.


Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

Major Specific Criteria


This articulation agreement displays lower-division course requirements specific to the major. Cal State LA lower-division course numbers range from 1000 - 2999. Students are advised to seek advisement from a counselor when planning to transfer to CSU Los Angeles and refer to the University Catalog to learn more about this major and its features. Additional admissions criteria for the major can be found on the Major Specific Criteria campus website. Please note that admissions requirements can vary by term so check back to see if there are any changes.

The Information Systems Department's responsibility is to educate its students in all aspects of organizational information systems and technology. The Department is engaged in teaching not just the design, development, implementation, and operation of information systems but also the management of such systems. The Department prepares its students for professional jobs in Information Systems. 


A total of 120-semester units is required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Information Systems, of which 43 units are in General Education courses. Consult an advisor for details on the specific number of units required in all areas of the degree, including GE, options, and electives.


This program offers three options:


1. Cybersecurity Option - Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting critical systems and sensitive information from digital attacks. Also known as Information Systems Security, Cybersecurity measures are designed to combat threats against networked systems and applications, whether those threats originate from inside or outside an organization. The Cybersecurity option in Information Systems (IS) provides students with the specialized knowledge needed for employment in Cybersecurity related jobs in businesses and government organizations. This option also offers elective courses that will allow the students to choose and acquire additional and supplementary knowledge of various IT fields, including but not limited to Enterprise Systems, Business Intelligence and Data Analytics, Application Development, Computer Networking, and Current Issues in Information Technology. Please contact the College of Business Advisement Center for more information. This option requires 15 units of option-specific required courses and 15 units of elective courses.


2. Data Analytics and AI Option - This option prepares students to harness data and artificial intelligence (AI) to solve real-world challenges, enhance decision-making, and drive innovation. Students gain a strong foundation in data analytics—learning how to describe, interpret, and predict outcomes—while also developing the ability to use AI tools that make analysis faster, more accurate, and more insightful. Through hands-on practice, case studies, and discussions of ethics and strategy, students learn how analytics and AI work together to uncover patterns, generate solutions, and shape the future of organizations. Graduates are well-prepared for careers that require strong data and AI skills in business, government, and technology.  This option also offers elective courses that will allow students to choose and acquire additional and supplementary knowledge of various IT fields, including but not limited to Cyber Security, Business Intelligence and Data Analytics, Application Development, Enterprise Systems, and Computer Networking. Please contact the College of Business Advisement Center for more information. This option requires 15 units of option-specific required courses and 15 units of elective courses.


3. Information Technology - This option prepares students to design, develop, and manage enterprise applications that power organizations in the digital age. The curriculum emphasizes web and e-business development, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, cloud computing, and low/no-code application design. By focusing on modern IT and enterprise solutions, students gain both technical expertise and problem-solving skills to meet the evolving demands of today’s employers. They also develop cross-functional knowledge in Accounting, Management, Marketing, and Finance—enabling them to deliver integrated IT solutions that streamline operations, improve customer experiences, and enhance organizational agility. This option also offers elective courses that will allow students to acquire supplemental knowledge of various IT fields, including but not limited to Cyber Security, Business Intelligence and Data Analytics, Enterprise Systems, and Computer Networking. Please contact the College of Business Advisement Center for more information. This option requires 15 units of option-specific required courses and 15 units of elective courses.
